blocks.content: Economic reforms refer to the changes introduced by the government to improve the efficiency and competitiveness of the economy. In India, major economic reforms were introduced in 1991 to overcome the severe economic crisis and promote economic growth.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The 1991 Economic Reforms were triggered by a severe Balance of Payments crisis and high inflation.
Liberalization dismantled the License Raj, removing industrial licensing for most sectors.
Privatization promoted disinvestment in Public Sector Enterprises to enhance market efficiency.
Globalization integrated India with the world economy by lowering trade barriers and encouraging FDI.
The New Economic Policy marked a structural shift from a command economy to a market-driven economy.

blocks.content: • In 1991, India faced a severe economic crisis.
• Foreign exchange reserves were very low.
• The government introduced economic reforms to stabilize the economy.
• The reforms aimed to promote liberalization, privatization and globalization.
• Liberalization refers to the removal of government restrictions on economic activities.
• It reduces government control over industries.
• Privatization means transferring ownership of public sector enterprises to private sector.
Economic Reforms in India: Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization.
• It reduces the financial burden on the government.
• Globalization refers to the integration of the Indian economy with the world economy.
• It promotes international trade and investment.
• It allows foreign companies to invest in India.

rows: Strict 'License Raj' regime required government permits for industry setup and expansion.
Abolished for almost all sectors, encouraging private enterprise.
Highly restricted with low ceiling limits and complex approval processes.
Opened up with automatic approval routes and relaxed FDI caps across sectors.
High import duties, quotas, and protective trade barriers.
Reduced import tariffs, removal of quantitative restrictions, and promotion of exports.
Dominant presence reserved across major economic and industrial activities.
Disinvestment of government equity and reduced reservation for state monopolies.

items: 1991 Crisis Context: Foreign exchange reserves fell to barely two weeks of imports, prompting emergency assistance from the IMF.
Rao-Manmohan Model: P.V. Narasimha Rao was the Prime Minister and Dr. Manmohan Singh was the Finance Minister during the 1991 NEP launch.
License Raj Abolition: Industrial licensing was eliminated for all except a small list of strategic and hazardous industries.
Banking & Monetary Reforms: The Narasimham Committee recommendations led to interest rate deregulation and lower CRR/SLR requirements.

blocks.content: • Economic reforms in India started in 1991.
• The reforms are based on LPG policy.
• LPG stands for Liberalization, Privatization and Globalization.
